title: General Pediatrics Fellowship
level: Academic General Pediatrics (AGP) scholarly research fellowship; physician and doctoral researchers; not an ACGME clinical subspecialty fellowship and not a general pediatrics residency.-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Completed medical degree/residency-level pediatrics background for physicians; this is a self-study curriculum and does not assess clinical competence.
Introductory epidemiology/statistics; basic spreadsheet literacy.
For doctoral research learners, knowledge of their home discipline and supervised institutional research training.
No access to patient records or clinical procedures is required or authorized.
objectives: Distinguish the Hopkins academic general pediatrics research fellowship from residency, ACGME subspecialty fellowship, directory label, and ABP certification.
Frame child primary-care research questions with community input and explicit population, measures, comparator, and time.
Select and critique study design, population data, measures, uncertainty, and causal claims.
Plan equity-aware community engagement, ethical safeguards, data governance, and scholarly dissemination.
Draft a protocol synopsis and improvement/implementation plan while stating limits and review needs.

units.title: Academic general pediatrics: scope, populations, and scholarly identity
objectives: Distinguish an AGP research fellowship from a general pediatrics residency, ACGME clinical subspecialty fellowship, and ABP exam.
Describe child primary care/population health research as evidence-to-practice and policy work.
State limits of institution-directory labels and accreditation claims.
topics: AGP scope; primary care/population health; question-to-policy pathway; physician and PhD routes.
boardDomains: No separate AGP board blueprint/domain exists. For physician learners, link only to relevant general-pediatrics clinical content in the current ABP General Pediatrics Content Outline; research methods are not represented as a separately tested ABP domain.

units.assessment: Review Hopkins page and identify what “80% research time” does and does not establish.

units.title: Researchable child-health questions and conceptual frameworks
objectives: Translate a community-prioritized problem into a focused, answerable question.
Specify population, exposure/intervention, comparator, outcome, setting, and time horizon.
Build a simple conceptual model without assuming causality.
topics: PICO/PECO; logic models; stakeholder priorities; outcomes; feasibility.
boardDomains: No separate AGP board blueprint/domain exists. For physician learners, link only to relevant general-pediatrics clinical content in the current ABP General Pediatrics Content Outline; research methods are not represented as a separately tested ABP domain.

units.assessment: Draft one primary-care research question and a one-page logic model; peer critique scope and equity.

units.title: Study designs, causal inference, and epidemiologic measures
objectives: Match cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, randomized, and pragmatic designs to the question.
Calculate and interpret risks/rates, prevalence, incidence, risk difference/ratio, and odds ratios at a conceptual level.
Identify selection, information, and confounding threats.
topics: Design taxonomy; target population; denominators; temporality; causal diagrams; bias.

units.assessment: Critique a CDC report: define population, denominator, time window, design, and one plausible bias.

units.title: Population health data, sampling, and surveillance
objectives: Distinguish clinical, administrative, survey, and surveillance datasets.
Evaluate coverage, sampling frame, missingness, representativeness, and ecological inference.
Select a defensible denominator and identify limits of small-area inference.
topics: Population-based data; sampling; weighted surveys; surveillance; linkage and ecological fallacy.

units.title: Health equity, community engagement, and participatory research
objectives: Separate disparity description from causal attribution and inequity analysis.
Plan community co-design, shared governance, accessible consent/communication, and return of results.
Explain structural context and avoid essentializing race or identity.
topics: Community-based participatory research; structural determinants; inclusion; power sharing; interpretation.

units.title: Measurement, patient-reported outcomes, EHR data quality

Assess reliability, validity, responsiveness, measurement invariance, and missingness.

topics: Constructs; validated measures; PROs; administrative code validity; data standards and linkage.

objectives: Distinguish effect estimate, confidence interval, and p-value.

units.assessment: Deliver a 3-minute public-facing research briefing and a one-page limitations statement.

assignment.title: Community-informed pediatric primary-care research protocol synopsis
deliverables: Two-page question and rationale with population, setting, estimand, conceptual model, partner/stakeholder plan.
Design/analysis brief: selection, measurement, denominator, confounding, missing data, precision and sensitivity issues.
Ethics/data governance/IRB decision points (no real data or recruitment).
Dissemination and implementation plan including plain-language return of results and explicit limitations.

rubric.levels: Exemplary: focused, actionable, community-prioritized; adequate: coherent but broad; needs revision: unsupported or infeasible.
Exemplary: design/estimand/measures/denominator align and uncertainty/bias addressed; adequate: minor mismatch; needs revision: causal overclaim or missing core definitions.

rubric.criterion: Equity, engagement, ethics and data governance
rubric.levels: Exemplary: power-sharing, child safeguards, privacy and institutional review are explicit; adequate: major elements present; needs revision: tokenizing or assumes approval/exemption.
Exemplary: roles, data definitions, QC, milestones and reproducibility clear; adequate: plausible but incomplete; needs revision: no credible workflow.
Exemplary: audience-appropriate, uncertainty honest, sources traceable; adequate: understandable with limited caveats; needs revision: unsubstantiated certainty or unclear sources.

formative: Unit reading checks and methods critique.
Ten original questions in this curriculum; not official ABP items and not psychometrically validated.
Peer review of a draft question and a CDC case report.
assessment.summative: Capstone protocol synopsis plus a short oral defense of design, uncertainty, equity, privacy and limits.
assessment.rubricWeights: Capstone criteria total 100%: question/feasibility 20; design and quantitative reasoning 25; equity/ethics/data governance 25; reproducibility/quality 15; communication/limitations 15.
assessment.passOrCertificationClaim: No passing score predicts board outcomes; completion is not a credential or training sign-off.

studyHours.basis: Transparent self-study plan, not institutional fellowship time: observed public lectures 20.94 h; reading and guided notes 18 h; case/report critique 10 h; assignments and peer review 18 h; review/reflection 5.06 h. These non-video hours are learning-plan estimates, never included in verified video-hour metrics.

unitMap.text: Academic general pediatrics: scope, populations, and scholarly identity
coveredTopics: AGP scope; primary care/population health; question-to-policy pathway; physician and PhD routes.

unitMap.text: Researchable child-health questions and conceptual frameworks
coveredTopics: PICO/PECO; logic models; stakeholder priorities; outcomes; feasibility.

unitMap.text: Study designs, causal inference, and epidemiologic measures
coveredTopics: Design taxonomy; target population; denominators; temporality; causal diagrams; bias.

unitMap.text: Population health data, sampling, and surveillance
coveredTopics: Population-based data; sampling; weighted surveys; surveillance; linkage and ecological fallacy.

unitMap.text: Health equity, community engagement, and participatory research
coveredTopics: Community-based participatory research; structural determinants; inclusion; power sharing; interpretation.

unitMap.text: Measurement, patient-reported outcomes, EHR data quality
coveredTopics: Constructs; validated measures; PROs; administrative code validity; data standards and linkage.

unitMap.text: Biostatistics, inference, randomization, and power
coveredTopics: Hypothesis testing; estimates; uncertainty; randomization; interaction; multiplicity; power.

unitMap.text: Secondary data, evidence synthesis, and reproducibility
coveredTopics: Secondary data; meta-analysis; inclusion/exclusion; missingness; reproducibility.

unitMap.text: Quality improvement and implementation science
coveredTopics: Model for Improvement/PDSA; process/outcome/balancing measures; implementation determinants; fidelity/adaptation.

unitMap.text: Human subjects, ethics, consent, and pediatric safeguards
coveredTopics: Human subjects; child assent/permission; privacy; IRB; equitable selection; data minimization.

unitMap.text: Protocols, project management, data governance, and quality
coveredTopics: Aims; protocol; operations manual; budget; roles; version control; data quality.

unitMap.text: Dissemination, policy translation, and scholarly communication
coveredTopics: Reporting checklists; community return of results; knowledge translation; policy communication.

topicGaps: The 36-hour verified public-video floor is met (37.6775 h; 1.6775 h above target); this is not a claim of board readiness, clinical competence, or clinical training equivalence.

The NIH lecture series is general clinical-research education rather than a pediatric primary-care fellowship curriculum. Unit mapping is topical, not a claim that recordings teach pediatric-specific standards or reproduce Johns Hopkins seminars.

Additional pediatric primary-care instruction remains needed on age/language measurement invariance, pediatric patient-reported measures, EHR capture of care outside one network, pediatric population-data linkage, and community co-governance in local settings.

Current clinical recommendations, applicable child-research rules, institutional review determinations, privacy requirements, and data-use approvals must be confirmed with authoritative sources and the responsible institution; self-study cannot supply approval or legal advice.

No separate academic general pediatrics board blueprint or certification was identified. General pediatrics ABP content is contextual only; research competencies are not an independently tested AGP board domain.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A team notices that children who live farther from a clinic have fewer preventive visits. Which next step most improves interpretability before calling this an access disparity?

options.text: Assume distance caused the lower visit rate.
Define the population, denominator, observation period, and how distance and visits are measured.
Exclude children with missing visits and ignore them.
Convert the finding to an odds ratio.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A descriptive association requires valid denominators and operational definitions before causal or equity claims. Consider coverage, visit capture, and confounding.

practiceQuestions.stem: A retrospective cohort estimates that a reminder intervention is associated with a 12 percentage-point increase in vaccination. The confidence interval ranges from -2 to +26 percentage points. Which is best?

options.text: The intervention is proven ineffective.
The result is compatible with effects ranging from small harm/no benefit to substantial benefit; uncertainty is high.
The intervention works in 12% of every population.
The p-value establishes practical importance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A wide interval crossing the null indicates imprecision; it does not prove no effect. Generalizability and design limitations also matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A study asks whether a new parent text-message program improves well-child attendance. Which design most directly estimates a causal effect if ethical and feasible?

options.text: Cross-sectional survey of parents who attend.
Randomized assignment of clinics or families with prespecified outcome and analysis.
Ecological comparison of county rates without adjustment.
Case series of three families.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Randomization can reduce confounding on average; design, clustering, consent, contamination and implementation still require planning.

practiceQuestions.stem: In an EHR study, children missing a follow-up visit are more likely to have moved or changed insurance. What is the main concern?

options.text: Missingness is automatically random.
Differential follow-up may bias estimates and reduce representativeness.
Missing visits increase specificity.
A larger sample fixes the bias.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Loss to follow-up related to exposure/outcome or determinants can cause selection bias; examine mechanisms and sensitivity.

practiceQuestions.stem: A community advisory group identifies language barriers as a research priority. Which approach best reflects participatory research?

options.text: Ask the group to approve a finished manuscript.
Share decision-making about question, measures, interpretation, and return of results from the outset.
Use the group only to recruit participants.
Remove community members from data interpretation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Meaningful partnership includes shared influence, transparent roles, and reciprocal dissemination, not token consultation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A team compares county-level poverty and asthma emergency visits and concludes that individual children in low-income households are at higher risk. What reasoning error is likely?

options.text: Lead-time bias.
Ecological fallacy: group-level associations do not establish individual-level associations.
Allocation concealment.
Recall bias.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Aggregate data support area-level analysis only unless linked/individual data support individual inference.

practiceQuestions.stem: A scale has high internal consistency. What cannot be concluded from this alone?

options.text: Items are correlated.
The measure is valid for every age, language, and construct.
Reliability needs further assessment.
Construct validity is a separate question.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Internal consistency alone does not establish validity, responsiveness, measurement invariance, or suitability across settings.

practiceQuestions.stem: A QI team makes a small process change to reduce missed follow-up in one clinic. What is the soundest first step regarding research oversight?

options.text: Declare every QI activity exempt from IRB.
Ask the institution’s designated office whether the project is QI, research, or both and what review is required before data collection.
Publish patient-level data to invite feedback.
Randomize children without consent.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The classification depends on intent, design, and applicable institutional/federal rules; the responsible office determines oversight.

practiceQuestions.stem: A non-significant difference between groups is reported. Which conclusion is defensible?

options.text: The groups are equivalent.
No evidence of a difference was detected; precision, design, power, and clinically important effects must be considered.
The null hypothesis is true.
The study proves harm is absent.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A failure to reject is not proof of equivalence; prespecified margins and design would be needed to claim equivalence/noninferiority.

practiceQuestions.stem: A pediatric research team plans to reuse EHR data for a new project. Which action is most appropriate before starting?

options.text: Assume all existing data are public.
Consult institutional privacy/data-governance and IRB or other designated review offices; minimize data and follow approvals.
Copy records to personal cloud storage.
Remove names and assume re-identification risk is zero.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Secondary use still involves privacy/security and potentially human-subjects determinations; de-identification does not guarantee zero risk.

title: Medicine-Pediatrics Urban Health Residency Program

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Advanced medical/health-professions learner with prior anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, clinical epidemiology, and supervised clinical foundations; best used as an evidence-navigation supplement by trainees/clinicians. Not an entry-to-practice course.
prerequisites: Basic adult and pediatric biomedical sciences
Ability to read clinical guideline tables and research summaries
Foundational ethics/privacy knowledge; review local rules under supervision before any clinical application
prerequisites.sequence: Take Units 1–4 as shared life-course/clinical foundations, then Units 5–11, and complete Unit 12 synthesis. Revisit live guideline dates throughout.

objectives: Explain that the institutional offering is an ACGME-listed (per JHM program page) four-year combined physician residency with an urban-health curriculum emphasis, not a separate specialty or board.
Map adult and pediatric diagnostic, preventive, acute, chronic and life-course content to the separate ABIM and ABP public blueprints.
Use current authoritative sources, identify guideline version/population, and communicate uncertainty.
Develop respectful plans for continuity, transition, substance use, behavioral health, HIV/HCV/STI, community partnership, carceral care and older-adult primary care.
Analyze authentic de-identified safety-event material only within repository access/copyright limits; never copy protected patient records or images.
Design a bounded educational assessment/QI proposal without claiming clinical competence or patient outcome results.

units.title: Med-Peds identity, life-course care, and cross-setting reasoning
objectives: Distinguish a combined physician residency from a named track and from an independent specialty/board.
Compare age-specific differences in adult and pediatric histories, examination, risk, consent, and family involvement.
Build a problem representation and prioritized differential without collapsing age-specific evidence.
topics: Combined internal medicine and general pediatrics scope; longitudinal primary care; inpatient/outpatient interfaces; age-based physiology; family-centered versus adult-centered care; continuity.
boardDomains: ABIM Internal Medicine domains and universal clinical tasks
ABP domains 1–24 and universal tasks: physiology, risk assessment, diagnosis, management
units.casePractice: Compare two explicitly fictional encounters (one adolescent, one older adult) and show how age, context, and longitudinal record alter the reasoning; do not treat educational cases as clinical advice.
units.assessment: Submit a two-column age-aware problem representation, differential, and safety-net plan; rubric: clinical distinctions 40%, evidence/task mapping 25%, reasoning and uncertainty 25%, clarity 10%.

units.title: Prevention, screening, immunization, and anticipatory guidance across ages
objectives: Select age- and risk-appropriate prevention questions using current source tables rather than memory alone.
Distinguish screening, diagnostic testing, surveillance, and counseling; identify when guidance is conditional or shared decision-making.
Explain how prevention changes from infant well visits to adult primary care and older age.
topics: Well-child and adult preventive care; growth and development; nutrition; tobacco/substance use; immunization schedule navigation; screening intervals and exceptions; counseling and vaccine hesitancy.
boardDomains: ABP D1 Preventative Pediatrics/Well-Child Care (12%); D3 Adolescent Care; D23 Ethics
ABIM prevention as cross-cutting content; risk assessment, diagnosis/testing, treatment/care decisions
units.casePractice: Use a de-identified case from AHRQ only if it illustrates prevention/safety; otherwise use a fictional vignette and calculate what reference table must be checked. No patient records or images.
units.assessment: Create a one-page adult/pediatric preventive-care decision map, date-stamp every schedule/USPSTF item, identify uncertainty; rubric: accurate source/version use 40%, age-specific distinctions 25%, risk/benefit nuance 25%, attribution 10%.

units.title: Acute illness, inpatient medicine, and escalation across the lifespan
objectives: Construct an initial problem list and illness-severity assessment for a child and an adult with undifferentiated symptoms.
Choose the next discriminating history, examination, or test and interpret results with age-appropriate pretest probability.
Identify red flags, resuscitation/escalation needs, handoff content, and limits of remote self-study.
topics: Undifferentiated fever, respiratory distress, shock warning signs, dehydration, altered mental status, acute kidney injury, chest pain, sepsis differential, transitions to higher level of care, discharge safety.
boardDomains: ABP D7 Emergency and Critical Care; D2 Fetal and Neonatal Care where relevant
ABIM cardiovascular, pulmonary, infectious disease, nephrology, neurology, diagnosis/testing and treatment tasks
units.casePractice: Work from an openly linked, anonymized WebM&M case for system-level failure analysis when available; for diagnosis use a constructed fictional case. Do not infer unseen vitals or invent imaging.
units.assessment: Submit a differential-and-escalation memo with a structured handoff; rubric: danger recognition 30%, test selection 25%, adult/pediatric distinctions 20%, communication and uncertainty 25%.

units.title: Chronic disease, multimorbidity, and longitudinal adult/pediatric primary care
objectives: Integrate chronic illness follow-up and competing risks in outpatient medicine and pediatrics.
Explain how developmental stage, caregiver role, and changing physiology affect chronic disease management.

units.title: Infectious diseases, HIV/HCV, STI, and TB in urban communities
objectives: Use exposure, host factors, epidemiology, and age to build a focused infectious differential.

units.title: Addiction medicine, opioid use disorder, and harm reduction
objectives: Use nonstigmatizing universal screening and brief assessment concepts for alcohol and drug use, including adolescents and adults.
Compare the roles of methadone, buprenorphine, and naltrexone as described by current official guidance; identify when specialist/emergency support is needed.
Plan a linkage/referral and continuity approach that accounts for pregnancy, co-occurring illness, overdose risk, and transitions of care.
topics: OUD, overdose prevention, MOUD access pathways, stigma, recovery supports, alcohol and stimulant use, chronic pain, adolescent risk, harm reduction, referral and follow-up.
boardDomains: ABP D5 Mental and Behavioral Health, D6 Psychosocial Issues, D24 Patient Safety/QI
ABIM psychiatry, infectious disease, ethics, substance-use disorders as cross-cutting topics; ABIM diagnosis/treatment/risk tasks
units.casePractice: For authentic safety cases, AHRQ WebM&M has anonymously reported real errors; discuss only the published de-identified account and do not reprint linked third-party copyrighted material. OUD learner cases are otherwise fictional.

units.title: Psychiatry, behavioral health, suicide-risk response, and trauma-informed care
objectives: Distinguish screening from assessment and diagnosis for depression, anxiety, substance use, trauma, and suicidality.
Identify urgent safety concerns and escalation roles without relying on a score alone.
Demonstrate trauma-informed, culturally responsive, developmentally appropriate communication.
topics: Adult psychiatric illness; adolescent mental health; dual diagnosis; violence exposure; adverse childhood experiences; safety planning principles; behavioral health integration; referral and continuity.
boardDomains: ABP D5 Mental and Behavioral Health (6%), D6 Psychosocial Issues (3%), D8 Child Abuse and Neglect, D23 Ethics

units.title: Housing insecurity, community medicine, and social-care navigation
objectives: Explain how housing instability, food, transport, safety, coverage, and structural conditions may affect access and continuity without reducing a person to a social label.
Map referral and community partnership processes and distinguish them from clinical treatment or program guarantees.
Design a respectful, opt-in question and an actionable follow-up workflow.
topics: Homelessness and health; community resource mapping; FQHC model; care coordination; barriers to care; street/community outreach; advocacy; local public-health partners; ethical documentation.
boardDomains: ABP D6 Psychosocial Issues, D23 Ethics, D24 Patient Safety/QI

units.casePractice: Use a published AHRQ WebM&M anonymous event for a safety lens only; otherwise build a fictional referral vignette. No images, patient charts or identifiable stories are copied. HRSA pages are program descriptions, not proof of individual-site resources.
units.assessment: Create a neighborhood-level resource map and a respectful referral workflow; rubric: specificity without overclaiming 30%, patient autonomy 25%, feasibility/continuity 25%, source quality 20%.

units.title: Carceral medicine, care continuity, and reentry

topics: Hopkins published carceral medicine experience; detention-health context; continuity of MOUD and chronic disease; HIV/TB follow-up; discharge/reentry; confidentiality and consent; ethical boundaries.

units.title: Adolescent, reproductive, sexual, gender-diverse, and family-centered care

assignment.title: Urban life-course continuity capstone (educational; do not use real patient data)
deliverables: A 1,200–1,800 word fictional composite case analysis spanning one pediatric/adolescent-to-adult transition or an adult-to-community transition; label all constructed details as fictional.
A two-board blueprint mapping: at least four ABP domains and four ABIM domains with task type; explain why this is not a single combined board exam.
A one-page transition/community referral map with a local-resource verification checklist; do not imply availability until confirmed.
A 90-day proposed process measure and balancing measure for follow-up; no claimed results and no patient-identifiable data.
A 5-minute oral defense with uncertainty, ethics/privacy, and safety escalation boundaries.

rubric.criterion: Clinical reasoning, developmental and adult/pediatric distinctions
Patient-centered urban context, ethics and feasible continuity

formative: 12-unit retrieval checks using the 10 original practice questions plus discussion prompts; questions are not official ABIM/ABP content.

topicGaps: Actual recording ledger: 16.53250 verified hours out of 36.00; 19.46750 hours remain. Scripted episodes and production plans are not rendered recordings and reduce no part of the gap.

Recorded teaching is concentrated in infectious disease/TB and addiction, plus one 2016 IBD transition recording and a 2025 adolescent HIV grand round. The 2022 HIV/STI/TB event and older material require current guideline checks; dated clips remain historical teaching, not current practice.

No verified recording coverage was found for broad adult IM blueprint domains (cardiometabolic, renal, pulmonary, rheumatology, hematology, neurology, etc.) or broad ABP domains beyond pediatric TB/HIV.

Material gaps remain in prevention and immunization schedule navigation; undifferentiated adult and pediatric acute care; general chronic multimorbidity and medication safety; HIV/HCV/STI current management; behavioral health and suicide response; housing insecurity/community resource navigation; carceral medicine/reentry; adolescent reproductive/gender-diverse care; geriatrics; and equity/QI/research methods.

Public JHM pages describe the Urban Health program and curriculum but do not supply a complete public institutional lecture catalogue or full didactic schedule; the independent course is not the JHM curriculum.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Internal Medicine certification examination
American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — General Pediatrics certifying examination
medical.boardStatus: Combined internal medicine-pediatrics training can support eligibility for two separate certifications from ABIM and ABP after qualifying ACGME-accredited training and satisfaction of each board’s current rules. This is not a separate “Med-Peds” or “Urban Health” board exam. The Urban Health designation is an institutional program emphasis/track, not an independent board specialty. The course is non-credit self-study and creates no eligibility.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Eligibility is determined solely by ABIM/ABP and depends on meeting all current requirements, including accredited graduate medical education, licensing and application rules. Completion of this independent course does not establish, replace, or imply board eligibility, supervised clinical experience, licensure, examination readiness, certification, or exam passing.

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
officialProgrammes.name: Medicine-Pediatrics Urban Health Residency Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official program page identifies a 4-year ACGME-accredited combined internal medicine-pediatrics physician residency and urban primary-care focus; program home/curriculum describe community medicine, addiction medicine, psychiatry, HIV/HCV, homelessness, carceral medicine, geriatrics and women’s health. Public pages do not expose a complete official lecture catalogue or full internal didactic schedule.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet names one distinct institutional program. Official JHM pages identify it as a physician residency and its Urban Health program/curriculum; it is not a research-only postdoctoral job, non-physician supplement, or generic directory category. ACGME status and duration are reported as shown on JHM’s public program page; the public ACGME program-finder entry was not independently inspected in this run. Exact institutional name preserved. The curriculum below is an independent learning design inspired by public materials, not the JHM curriculum itself.
sourceCaveats: JHM program and curriculum pages are institution-authored descriptions. The official page says ACGME accredited and four years, but public source availability did not permit independent ACGME ADS verification for this exact program in this pass.
ACGME requirements are effective 2026 standards; a requirement document is not evidence of local teaching hours, trainee experience, or completed accreditation review.
ABIM/ABP public certification policies change; verify the board sites for the learner’s cohort and current examination application rules.
The ABP 2024 and ABIM January 2026 blueprints are distinct assessment specifications; they do not equal a full training curriculum or estimate likelihood of passing.

CDC immunization schedules are unusually date-sensitive. Pages fetched on 2026-10-07 displayed a July 2, 2025 schedule and a court-stay notice; verify live legal status, addenda and agency recommendations before any real use.
CDC STI guideline cited here is 2021 and includes an erratum; verify the current CDC updates before clinical use.
NIH HIV guidance is updated frequently; adult/adolescent and pediatric recommendations are distinct; source pages warn guidelines cannot cover every scenario.
SAMHSA TIP 63 is a 2021 publication; check current FDA labeling, regulations, guidance, patient context and specialist supervision.
AHRQ WebM&M current individual-case access was not verified. Its page says anonymous case reports are expert analyzed and warns linked third-party materials may require permission before reprinting.
Free-to-view is not permission to copy, rehost, or redistribute; course references link only to original sources. No patient-level data, case images, or source media were copied.
No clinical peer review was conducted. All practice scenarios developed here are educational and not individualized advice.

topicGaps: Actual recording ledger: 16.53250 verified hours out of 36.00; 19.46750 hours remain. Scripted episodes and production plans are not rendered recordings and reduce no part of the gap.

Recorded teaching is concentrated in infectious disease/TB and addiction, plus one 2016 IBD transition recording and a 2025 adolescent HIV grand round. The 2022 HIV/STI/TB event and older material require current guideline checks; dated clips remain historical teaching, not current practice.

No verified recording coverage was found for broad adult IM blueprint domains (cardiometabolic, renal, pulmonary, rheumatology, hematology, neurology, etc.) or broad ABP domains beyond pediatric TB/HIV.

Material gaps remain in prevention and immunization schedule navigation; undifferentiated adult and pediatric acute care; general chronic multimorbidity and medication safety; HIV/HCV/STI current management; behavioral health and suicide response; housing insecurity/community resource navigation; carceral medicine/reentry; adolescent reproductive/gender-diverse care; geriatrics; and equity/QI/research methods.

Public JHM pages describe the Urban Health program and curriculum but do not supply a complete public institutional lecture catalogue or full didactic schedule; the independent course is not the JHM curriculum.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner is asked to characterize the Johns Hopkins Medicine-Pediatrics Urban Health offering. Which description is best supported by its public program page?

options.text: A non-physician research supplement with no clinical residency.
A four-year ACGME-accredited combined internal medicine-pediatrics physician residency with an urban-health emphasis.
A distinct Urban Health board specialty with one combined exam.
A one-year elective independent of categorical residency.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official program page identifies the Johns Hopkins Hospital, ACGME accreditation, four-year duration and an innovative combined internal medicine-pediatrics residency; it emphasizes inner-city primary care. There is no separate “urban health” board. This is institutional self-description, not verification of the candidate’s individual eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A resident has completed an approved four-year combined IM-Pediatrics residency and seeks certification. Which pathway is described by the boards?

options.text: One Med-Peds board examination grants both credentials automatically.
Only ABP certification is available after combined training.
ABIM and ABP offer dual certification, subject to each board’s requirements and satisfactory completion of accredited combined training.
A nonclinical Urban Health certificate substitutes for both board exams.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM states that ABIM and ABP offer dual certification, combined education is 48 months, ACGME combined accreditation is required, and candidates become eligible for certifying examination only after successful completion of accredited training. The learning program here confers none of those credentials.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 16-year-old with a chronic condition is expected to move to adult-centered care later. Which educational framework most directly structures preparation, readiness, planning, transfer and completion?

options.text: A single transfer letter on the day of the 18th birthday.
Got Transition’s Six Core Elements, used as a longitudinal process and adapted to the patient/practice.
A one-time adult board blueprint.
A new medication list without patient participation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Got Transition defines transition as planning, transfer and integration, with six elements from policy/guide through transition completion. The framework is a process, not an age-triggered one-time referral or guarantee of successful integration.

practiceQuestions.stem: A student reviews a vaccine question for a child and an adult. Which approach is most defensible for current clinical study?

options.text: Apply one static schedule to all ages.
Use a memorized schedule without checking notes or addenda.
Open the live age-appropriate CDC schedule, review medical-indication/catch-up notes and date/status, then verify the latest authoritative update.
Assume the ABP blueprint contains dose-specific vaccine instructions.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC schedules separate child/adolescent and adult tables and direct users to catch-up, medical-indication, notes, contraindications and addenda. Vaccine recommendations are date-sensitive; study with the current live pages. This item intentionally does not supply an individual recommendation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A person presents for an HIV-related discussion in an adult clinic, while a pediatric/adolescent case is also being considered. Which source-navigation statement is most accurate?

options.text: Adult/adolescent ART guidance applies identically to every child and prepubertal adolescent.
Use the current NIH adult/adolescent guideline for that population; consult separate pediatric guidance where applicable, and check live updates and clinical context.
HIV guidance does not change after publication.
PrEP is covered only by ART treatment guidelines.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NIH explicitly distinguishes adult/adolescent ART scope from pediatric ARV guidance and notes recommendations can change and do not cover every scenario. NIH also points to CDC for PrEP/PEP of people without HIV.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult patient says they may be using opioids nonmedically and asks about treatment. Which first educational step best reflects a nonstigmatizing, evidence-seeking approach?

options.text: Assume treatment means detoxification only and do not discuss medications.
Use respectful assessment, discuss that evidence-based options include methadone, buprenorphine and naltrexone, and connect the person with qualified local clinical care.
Tell the patient that one medication is always correct for every patient.
Require a lecture or abstinence period before offering referral.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SAMHSA TIP 63 reviews these three FDA-approved medications and other recovery supports. Choice among options requires individualized clinician assessment, current labeling and local treatment pathways; this question does not direct treatment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A resident finds a WebM&M safety case that links to a journal article containing additional material. What is the appropriate course use?

options.text: Copy all linked text into course notes because it is available on the web.
Use the AHRQ page as a link for case discussion and check permissions before reproducing third-party content.
Download and share any underlying patient chart.
Add a recognizable patient photograph to improve the lesson.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHRQ describes WebM&M as expert analysis of anonymously reported cases, while cautioning that permission to reprint linked non-AHRQ materials may require contacting the rights holder. Free-to-view is not permission to rehost.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient reports unstable housing and misses follow-up. Which response best fits an urban-health, patient-centered educational approach?

options.text: Document “noncompliant” and close the case.
Ask permission to explore practical barriers, co-design an actionable referral/continuity plan, and verify available services instead of assuming capacity.
Promise that every HRSA health center provides the same local services immediately.
Use housing status as a substitute for clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The program curriculum emphasizes community resources and reducing barriers. HRSA describes the national health-center model but does not establish capacity at a specific site. A respectful plan should be actionable and not overpromise.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the ABP general pediatrics content outline is correct?

options.text: It is only a list of lecture hours at Johns Hopkins.
It includes 24 content domains and four universal task categories to emphasize application of knowledge.
It replaces the ABIM internal-medicine blueprint for adult content.
It guarantees a learner will pass after completing all listed topics.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABP 2024 outline identifies 24 content domains and universal tasks (physiology/pathophysiology, epidemiology/risk, diagnosis, management/treatment). It is an exam content outline, not a residency or performance guarantee.

practiceQuestions.stem: An urban clinic team proposes improving completed follow-up after discharge. Which first step is most consistent with a quality-improvement learning assignment?

options.text: Announce success before collecting baseline data.
Define a measurable process/outcome and balancing measure, map the workflow, and plan an ethical small test before interpreting results.
Use identifiable patient records outside authorization to make a compelling chart.
Assume a national program description proves local performance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A small QI charter should identify a measurable aim and measures, including a balancing measure; data use requires appropriate permissions and privacy protections. Program descriptions are not local outcome evidence.

unitMap.text: Transition, neonatal physiology, and delivery-room stabilization
coveredTopics: Explain fetal-to-neonatal circulatory and respiratory transition and how it informs initial assessment.
Prioritize effective ventilation and interpret heart-rate response within current resuscitation guidance.
Distinguish knowledge assessment from hands-on NRP competence.

unitMap.text: Respiratory development, RDS, and lung-protective support
coveredTopics: Connect developmental lung physiology to surfactant-deficient RDS while considering alternative diagnoses.
Compare non-invasive respiratory support and invasive ventilation concepts without treating a guideline as a patient-specific order.
Evaluate evidence uncertainty and date of respiratory recommendations.

unitMap.text: Pulmonary vascular disease, BPD, and monitoring
coveredTopics: Relate pulmonary vascular physiology to hypoxemia and hemodynamic context.
Identify limits of echocardiography, lung ultrasound, NIRS, and surrogate endpoints.
Frame BPD-associated pulmonary hypertension as a multidisciplinary assessment problem.

unitMap.text: Neonatal cardiovascular physiology, PDA, congenital heart disease, and shock
coveredTopics: Integrate gestational age, perfusion, shunts, ventricular function, and transition when reasoning about cardiovascular instability.
Interpret PDA evidence cautiously and distinguish anatomical patency from hemodynamic significance.
Describe diagnostic roles and limits of targeted neonatal echocardiography and advanced imaging.

unitMap.text: Neurologic injury, seizures, neuroimaging, and developmental outcomes
coveredTopics: Describe differential diagnosis and evaluation domains for neonatal encephalopathy and seizures.
Distinguish evidence on established HIE treatment indications from unresolved questions in mild HIE.
Interpret neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental monitoring as multimodal rather than stand-alone diagnosis.

unitMap.text: Maternal-fetal medicine, prematurity, placenta, and perinatal risk
coveredTopics: Relate maternal illness, fetal growth, placental and delivery factors to neonatal presentations.
Explain why population-level outcome data do not determine an individual family's prognosis.
Compare stabilization needs with family-centered, culturally humble communication.

unitMap.text: Immunology, infection, sepsis, and antimicrobial stewardship
coveredTopics: Formulate an age- and context-sensitive infection differential using maternal and neonatal history.
Separate early clinical suspicion from confirmed microbiology and review antibiotic stewardship principles.
Recognize limitations of isolated physiologic markers and evolving sepsis evidence.

unitMap.text: Nutrition, gastrointestinal disease, bilirubin, and NEC
coveredTopics: Map enteral and parenteral nutrition principles to growth, feeding skills, and prematurity.
Distinguish unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia risk assessment from thresholds outside an applicable guideline's gestational-age scope.
Recognize GI emergencies and identify imaging interpretation limits.

unitMap.text: Water, electrolytes, renal, endocrine, metabolic, and thermal regulation
coveredTopics: Interpret neonatal fluid shifts, renal maturation, glucose homeostasis, and acid-base patterns.
Differentiate transitional hypoglycemia from persistent disease using age and clinical status.
Select data for a differential and identify when specialist evaluation is needed.

unitMap.text: Hematology, genetics, dysmorphology, skin, eye, and hearing
coveredTopics: Organize neonatal anemia, platelet, hemolysis, jaundice, and thrombosis differentials.
Use phenotype and family history to prioritize genetic testing questions without declaring a diagnosis.
Connect preventive screening and longitudinal follow-up with ROP, hearing, and developmental risk.

unitMap.text: Surgical and complex NICU care, pharmacology, ethics, and family partnership
coveredTopics: Synthesize multidisciplinary perioperative, analgesia, technology, transport, and co-management considerations.
Explain neonatal pharmacokinetic variability and why dosing must be checked against current local references and supervised care.
Use shared decision-making principles in prognostic uncertainty, serious news, and palliative care.

unitMap.text: Neonatal systems, QI, research literacy, and board-domain synthesis
coveredTopics: Appraise study design, effect estimates, bias, external validity, and changing evidence.
Design a small process-focused QI question with a measurable outcome and balancing measure.
Use all 17 ABP blueprint domains as a map while recognizing that this course does not validate board readiness.

topicGaps: No directly counted lecture unit for ABP Domains 5–6: nutrition, gastrointestinal disease, bilirubin, NEC and feeding.
No directly counted lecture unit for Domains 9–13: genetics, renal, endocrine/metabolic, hematology/oncology, EENT/skin/ROP/hearing.
Domain 4 has a sepsis lecture, but immunology, neonatal infection epidemiology and antibiotic stewardship do not have a comprehensive public lecture sequence.
Domain 7 maternal-fetal and prematurity exposure is only partially represented.
Domains 14–17 have limited targeted lecture depth for surgery, pharmacology, systems, communication, QI and research.

These content gaps remain despite 73.04 unique observed public-video hours because the available recordings cluster in cardiopulmonary and neurologic subjects. Planned clips are not counted as ready hours.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is a clinical physician subspecialty fellowship, not a generic directory category, combined programme, or non-physician track. BIDMC’s page describes post-residency clinical training plus mentored research. The Harvard GME page identifies the same shared Harvard Neonatal-Perinatal program, with BIDMC as one site and an associate director. BIDMC’s page names three sites; the current Harvard program page names four (adds MGH), so exact descriptions are preserved and the discrepancy is not resolved by inference. Post-fellowship research maturation is separate from the three-year physician fellowship. Packet names BIDMC; no separate Johns Hopkins programme was asserted or researched for this item. The 2026 ACGME requirements establish general accreditation rules but do not independently verify the current individual accreditation status of this named program; the official BIDMC page states exam eligibility after successful fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: During an attended birth, a newborn remains bradycardic after initial warming and stimulation. Which response best reflects current neonatal resuscitation priorities?

options.text: Focus first on effective lung ventilation and assess whether the heart rate rises.
Use pulse oximetry alone to determine heart rate and defer ventilation until saturation is known.
Begin compressions for any heart rate below 100/min before optimizing ventilation.
Assume most newborns require advanced resuscitation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: 2025 AHA/AAP guidance identifies effective ventilation, reflected by an increasing heart rate, as the priority; compressions have a more specific escalation threshold after effective ventilation and corrective steps. The question is educational, not an NRP certification item.

practiceQuestions.stem: A preterm infant at risk for RDS is breathing spontaneously and does not require intubation for stabilization. Which broad approach is consistent with the 2025 European consensus?

options.text: Start non-invasive respiratory support from birth and individualize escalation using ongoing assessment.
Intubate every infant at risk before observing respiratory effort.
Avoid oxygen monitoring because it is not part of RDS care.
Use a single surfactant threshold regardless of context or guideline.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current 2025 consensus update recommends non-invasive support from birth for at-risk infants who do not need intubation for stabilization, with individualized respiratory care; it is not a patient-specific protocol.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional at-risk newborn continues to have low glucose readings after 72 hours of age. Under the CPS statement updated in 2025, which framework is most appropriate?

options.text: Treat this as persistent hypoglycemia requiring further evaluation; obtain a critical sample when indicated by the statement.
Continue to label every low value transitional without considering age.
Use continuous glucose monitoring as a definitive substitute for confirmatory testing.
No follow-up is needed if the infant appears well.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The CPS statement distinguishes the first 72-hour transitional period from persistent hypoglycemia and recommends further evaluation for persistent low values, including an appropriately timed critical sample. Exact management depends on current local guidance and clinicians.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 34-week infant has jaundice. Which statement about the AAP 2022 hyperbilirubinemia guideline is correct?

options.text: Its treatment graphs are designed for infants at least 35 weeks; do not directly apply them below that gestational-age scope.
The graphs apply to all gestational ages and birthweights.
A transcutaneous value always eliminates the need for serum testing.
The guideline is retired and cannot be used in 2026.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AAP describes its 2022 guideline as applying to newborns ≥35 weeks and remaining valid through August 2027. The lower-gestation infant requires a different relevant protocol; this educational item does not supply one.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a hypothetical neonatal cardiovascular review, the team has one blood-pressure value and a patent ductus on echocardiography. What is the strongest reasoning next step?

options.text: Integrate gestational age, perfusion, shunt physiology, ventricular function, trends, and the measurement context before inferring significance.
Diagnose shock solely from the blood-pressure value.
Assume any PDA automatically requires closure.
Use one echo measurement as a stand-alone treatment indication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABP blueprint includes cardiovascular physiology and disorders; the public hemodynamic lectures frame integrated evaluation and PDA evidence as nuanced. Anatomy or one isolated metric does not establish a treatment indication.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educational conference discusses therapeutic hypothermia and mild neonatal encephalopathy. Which conclusion is best supported by cautious evidence appraisal?

options.text: Separate established eligibility frameworks from ongoing uncertainty; do not presume evidence for standard cooling of mild HIE.
All infants with any encephalopathy automatically meet identical eligibility.
A lecture title alone establishes a universal treatment recommendation.
Neuroimaging alone replaces clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The board outline includes HIE, and public lectures explicitly frame mild HIE as a clinical/evidence question. The course asks learners to distinguish established treatment criteria from emerging evidence; it does not state a patient-specific therapeutic recommendation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A QI team wants to reduce avoidable variation in a NICU process. Which initial plan best aligns with the ABP/ACGME scholarly and improvement domains?

options.text: Define the process, population, measurable outcome and balancing measure, then review data and change over time.
Change care immediately based on an anecdote and omit measurement.
Treat a single before-after observation as proof of causation.
Use an unvalidated test score to certify clinical competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP’s outline includes neonatal care systems, scholarly activity and QI; ACGME requires practice-based learning and improvement. A transparent aim, measurement strategy, and interpretation of limitations are appropriate learning tasks.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner links a neonatal radiograph from an online case archive into a public slide deck. What is the best rights-aware action?

options.text: Link to the source and verify de-identification and reuse permission; do not copy or rehost without an applicable license or permission.
Assume free viewing means public-domain reuse.
Remove the source credit and reuse the image.
Assume an old educational image has no copyright.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The University of Hawaii archive supplies authentic neonatal radiograph teaching cases but does not state an open reuse license or independent de-identification attestation on the page. Link-only use with rights checks avoids treating free viewing as reuse permission.
practiceQuestions.domain: 14 Surgical and Complex NICU Patient Management

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellow uses the ACGME Milestones document as a high-stakes credentialing examination for an independent online course. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: Milestones are formative tools for learners in accredited programs and are not designed as sole certification or credentialing evidence.
Milestone Level 4 automatically establishes independent practice competence.
Completing online questions creates ACGME fellowship credit.
A course may reproduce the institution’s assessment and claim equivalence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME milestone document expressly limits intended use to assessment in accredited programs; Level 4 is a graduation goal rather than a requirement, and the document warns against sole high-stakes use.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner follows the 2025 RDS consensus. Which statement best reflects the document’s scope and date?

options.text: It is a European consensus update published in 2026 using evidence through mid-2025; local protocols and patient context remain essential.
It is an AAP board examination blueprint.
It eliminates all uncertainty in respiratory support.

title: Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship

prerequisites.detail: Pediatrics residency-level knowledge of neonatal physiology, perinatal history, basic pharmacology, developmental biology, epidemiology and evidence appraisal; intended for physician trainees and supervised clinicians as academic self-study.

No patient-specific diagnostic, treatment, medication, resuscitation, feeding or procedural advice. Clinical decisions require appropriately trained professionals, supervision and current local protocols.
Prerequisites recommended for course comprehension are not board eligibility; see boardEligibilityNotice and official ABP rules.

objectives: Map the ABP outline’s 17 domains and four universal tasks to a structured self-study plan.
Explain normal perinatal and neonatal physiology and use it to generate—not overstate—clinical differentials.
Compare evidence and diagnostic limits for neonatal disease domains, considering gestational age, timing, risks, and clinical context.
Interpret open-access clinical literature with attention to population, outcomes, harms, uncertainty and guideline currency.
Distinguish public clinical programme descriptions, ACGME program standards, ABP exam blueprints and actual board eligibility.
Use case resources lawfully: link authentic de-identified published cases, follow license and consent terms, and never upload patient data.
Develop scholarly and QI questions with attention to ethics, health equity, systems and measures.

units.title: Core sciences, fetal development, placental physiology, and transition
objectives: Explain gestational-age-dependent maturation and transition from fetal to neonatal physiology across organ systems.
Relate maternal disease, medications, placental function, fetal growth, and delivery factors to neonatal risk without deterministic inference.
topics: embryology and developmental physiology
placental circulation and gas exchange
fetal surveillance, growth restriction, multiple gestation
transition at birth; delayed cord clamping concepts
units.casePractice: Build a causal diagram for a fictional pregnancy-to-transition vignette; annotate uncertainties and alternative explanations.
units.assessment: One-page annotated diagram scored for physiology (35%), evidence quality (25%), uncertainty (20%), and clarity (20%).

units.title: Respiratory disease, support, and chronic lung outcomes
objectives: Differentiate common respiratory mechanisms using history, examination, gas exchange, imaging concepts, and trajectory.
Explain evidence-based principles for RDS, surfactant, non-invasive support, air leaks, pulmonary hypertension, and BPD while deferring bedside actions to local supervision.
topics: lung development and transition
RDS and surfactant evidence
apnea, air leak, infection, airway disease
BPD/chronic lung disease; pulmonary vascular disease
boardDomains: 14 Surgical and Complex NICU Patient Management
units.casePractice: Create an evidence map comparing mechanism, diagnostic uncertainty, monitoring concept, and harms for two fictional respiratory courses.
units.assessment: Case analysis scored for domain breadth (30%), discriminating reasoning (30%), evidence update check (25%), and safety (15%).

units.title: Cardiovascular physiology and hemodynamic reasoning
objectives: Connect transitional circulation, shunts, myocardial function, rhythm, and pulmonary vascular resistance to observable patterns.
Describe the limits of screening, echo, blood pressure, and biomarkers and identify when multidisciplinary assessment is needed.
topics: transition and ductal physiology
hypotension/hypertension, heart failure, PDA
pulmonary hypertension, congenital disease, arrhythmia, tamponade
boardDomains: 14 Surgical and Complex NICU Patient Management
units.casePractice: Use a hypothetical trend set to separate observation, hypothesis, differential, and confirmatory data needs.
units.assessment: Reasoning grid scored for physiology (35%), differential (25%), test interpretation limits (25%), escalation (15%).

units.title: Neurology, seizures, HIE, and neurodevelopment
objectives: Describe normal neonatal neurologic assessment and how gestational age modifies interpretation.
Compare broad mechanisms and diagnostic domains for seizures, HIE, hemorrhage/ischemia, infection, and neuromuscular tone; distinguish acute care from long-term follow-up.
topics: neurologic examination and developmental surveillance
neonatal seizures and EEG concepts
HIE, hypoxic-ischemic injury, hemorrhage and stroke
neuromuscular conditions; high-risk follow-up
units.casePractice: Construct a fictional timeline that links perinatal events to differential and follow-up questions without making causal certainty claims.
units.assessment: Timeline scored for temporal logic (25%), differential (30%), test limits (20%), follow-up equity (25%).

units.title: Immunology, perinatal infection, and antimicrobial stewardship
objectives: Classify risk and timing concepts for early/late neonatal infection and perinatal viral/fungal disease.
Appraise diagnostic uncertainty, test performance, prevention, antimicrobial stewardship, and maternal-neonatal context.
topics: immune development
GBS, EOS/LOS, viral/fungal disease
infection prevention, vaccination context, stewardship
units.casePractice: Analyze a fictional sepsis-evaluation vignette using pretest probability, available evidence, harms, and local protocol caveat.
units.assessment: Short memo scored for evidence hierarchy (30%), diagnostic reasoning (30%), stewardship (20%), safety caveat (20%).

units.title: Nutrition, lactation, feeding, growth, and metabolic bone health
objectives: Explain principles of human milk, enteral/parenteral nutrition, supplements, oral-motor feeding, growth, and nutritional deficiency.

topics: maternal milk and lactation
parenteral and enteral nutrition
growth assessment, feeding and oral motor disorders
vitamin/mineral adequacy and osteopenia of prematurity
units.casePractice: Critique a fictional growth chart and nutrition history; list missing context before interpreting percentile change.
units.assessment: Chart critique scored for measures/context (35%), differential (25%), evidence (20%), communication (20%).

units.title: Gastroenterology, bilirubin, cholestasis, and surgical abdomen
objectives: Explain bilirubin metabolism and distinguish screening/management guidance by gestational-age scope.

topics: bilirubin physiology and AAP ≥35-week guideline boundary
NEC, intestinal obstruction/perforation, GI bleeding
cholestasis, hepatic failure, malformations
boardDomains: 14 Surgical and Complex NICU Patient Management
units.casePractice: Make a guideline-scope checklist for a fictional jaundiced infant with explicit gestational-age applicability and missing data.
units.assessment: Rubric: scope and age population (35%), differential (25%), evidence use (25%), caution (15%).

units.title: Resuscitation, stabilization, and ethics at birth
objectives: Summarize current guideline structure for preparation, initial assessment, respiratory support, and escalation principles.

topics: preparation and delivery-room stabilization
resuscitation sequence and ventilation concepts
perinatal asphyxia and post-resuscitation evaluation
ethics, palliative approach and shared decision-making
units.casePractice: Write a non-directive communication reflection from a fictional high-risk delivery scenario; use current NRP source to identify what requires certified team practice.
units.assessment: Rubric: correct guideline reference (30%), communication (25%), uncertainty (25%), scope/supervision (20%).

units.title: Genetics, congenital anomalies, and dysmorphology

prenatal diagnosis and postnatal testing
genetic counseling and family communication

units.title: Renal, fluids, electrolytes, acid-base, endocrine, metabolic, and thermal regulation

topics: water/salt balance, renal maturation and AKI
acid-base interpretation concepts
glucose, calcium/phosphorus/magnesium, thyroid/adrenal, IEM
thermal regulation and osteopenia
units.casePractice: Create a fictional lab-trend annotation separating observed data from cause hypotheses and listing urgent supervisor questions.
units.assessment: Rubric: physiology (30%), differential (25%), trend/sampling (25%), safety (20%).

units.title: Hematology, oncology, skin, eye, ear, head and neck
objectives: Compare neonatal anemia, hemolysis, polycythemia, platelet/coagulation abnormalities, and congenital infection implications.
Identify key domains of ROP, hearing, congenital anomalies, skin findings, and neonatal tumors without substituting for specialist evaluation.
topics: anemia and hemolytic disease
platelet and hemostasis problems; thrombosis
ROP/hearing/eye/EENT/skin and vascular lesions
congenital leukemia and solid tumors
units.casePractice: Use a linked authentic open case or a fictional case to document observation vs interpretation; do not download or copy clinical imagery.

units.title: Complex NICU care, pharmacology, systems, scholarship and QI
objectives: Describe perioperative/complex-care coordination, technologies, neonatal pharmacology principles, safe handoffs, and systems-based resource considerations.
Critically appraise research and design an ethical, measurable QI question while recognizing that course work is not ABP scholarly activity credit.
topics: perioperative and complex NICU care, ECMO/lines/devices as concepts
pharmacokinetics and neonatal drug disposition
transport, handoff, equity, leadership and care systems
biostatistics, epidemiology, ethics, QI and scholarship
boardDomains: 14 Surgical and Complex NICU Patient Management

assignment.title: Blueprint-linked neonatal reasoning and evidence portfolio
components: 12 unit outputs; one short source/uncertainty log per unit
three fictional case maps with observation/hypothesis/test distinctions
one systems/QI charter with measure, balancing measure, equity lens and safeguards
final 17-domain coverage map identifying strong and weak study areas
assignment.limits: Educational formative rubric only, not ABP assessment, clinical evaluation, official portfolio, scholarly work product approval or board-passing predictor.

assessment.formative: 12 unit checks, original 12-question set, evidence appraisal, portfolio and reflective gaps log. Suggested pass benchmark is 80% for repeated retrieval practice only; it is not validated, predictive, or an eligibility threshold.
assessment.summative: Self-scored blueprint map and revision plan; no exam credential.

topicGaps: Observed free recording time is 1.9672 hours against a 36-hour specialty video target; the exact residual gap is 34.0328 hours. Original episodes are scripts, not rendered recordings and contribute zero verified hours.

Only two verified recordings were found in the checked public catalog. The CDH talk covers complex care, transition and team systems; the nutrition talk covers feeding evidence and growth. They do not constitute complete coverage of those domains.

No duration- and access-verified recordings were available in this check for most of the 17 ABP domains, especially genetics/dysmorphology, renal and endocrine/metabolic disease, infection/immunology, hematology/oncology, dermatology/EENT, pharmacology, transport, research methods and QI.

The ABP 2022 content outline remains an exam blueprint, not a curriculum. Current clinical details require current source checks; individual domain subtopics and universal tasks need more primary-source-grounded instruction.

UF MediaSite recordings were inaccessible without university login, and the Cleveland Clinic playlists lacked an accessible item-level runtime ledger. Pediatrix item access may require CME portal interaction. These source gaps remain uncounted rather than assumed free.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine
medical.boardStatus: This is a real ABP pediatric subspecialty with a separate ABP Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine certifying examination and an ABP-published 17-domain content outline. The outline is an exam blueprint, not a full curriculum or study guide. This independent course confers no board credential. The RCPSC is noted by ABP as an alternative accredited training jurisdiction, but this U.S.-program course is not an RCPSC pathway.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABP page checked 2026-10-07: the ordinary route requires three years of full-time, broad-based Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine fellowship in an ACGME-accredited U.S. or RCPSC-accredited Canadian program, required General Pediatrics initial certification and maintenance (subject to ABP-stated pending-result exceptions), a valid unrestricted U.S./territory/Canadian medical license, program-director verification of training and competence/professionalism plus scholarly activity, and passing the separate subspecialty certifying examination. ABP rules on leave, part-time training, prior credit, transfer, time-limited eligibility and exceptional pathways may apply; confirm current rules with ABP. This course, lectures, assessments, research, or observership do not satisfy any eligibility requirement.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This MED-148 packet is one actual, named, joint clinical physician fellowship based at Boston Children’s Hospital—not a generic directory heading, not a non-physician course and not research-only postdoctoral employment. The program’s public overview identifies clinical NICU training across BCH, BWH, BIDMC and MGH; BCH CICU is a one-month rotation. These are exact hospital/site variants within one Harvard fellowship, not five distinct fellowships or five separate board credentials. Research/physician-scientist emphasis is part of the program, not a replacement for the clinical track. No combined internal medicine-pediatrics neonatal subspecialty pathway is asserted. The independent course is unaffiliated with Harvard or any site.
sourceCaveats: ABP exam blueprint effective March 1, 2022; ABP notes content outlines are not intended as curriculum or study guides and dynamic clinical details may change.

ACGME 2026 Neonatal-Perinatal requirements/FAQs include July 1, 2026 effective language and interim revisions; source is program standards, not a board blueprint. BCH’s official application page lists ACGME ID suffix 1028; AAMC ERAS lists Boston Children’s Hospital Program, ID 3292421028, as Participating on 2026-10-07. Directory status is not a guarantee of an individual’s acceptance or eligibility.
Harvard program overview/curriculum pages are public but are not a complete reusable collection of its protected teaching or evidence of exact hours.

Clinical guidance must be checked against current local protocols and live society/agency sources. AAP bilirubin page states the cited guideline is limited to infants ≥35 weeks and remains valid until August 2027.
Course is educational self-study and is not affiliated, accredited GME, clinical care, licensure, board eligibility/certification or procedure competence. No human clinical review was performed.
The case-report resource is linked rather than rehosted. Although CC BY is stated, image/data consent and attribution requirements still govern any reuse; no case material is copied here.

Pediatrix webinars may require CME portal interaction and/or registration. UF and Cleveland Clinic catalogs do not provide a completed item-level no-login/runtime ledger in this task. Seattle Children’s catalogue may list duration but its neonatal items were not verified one by one. No such entries count toward video hours.
